name: Muhammad ibn Bashshar, Bundar
nameAr: محمد بن بشار بن عثمان العبدي البصري، أبو بكر، بندار

verdicts.en: Acceptable; there is no harm in him.
A Basran, reliable, with many hadith.

verdicts.ar: حدثنا إمام أهل زمانه محمد بن بشار
verdicts.en: “The imam of the people of his age, Muhammad ibn Bashshar, narrated to us” (in Kitab al-Tawhid).

verdicts.ar: لم يرحل ففاته كبار، واقتنع بعلماء البصرة، أرجو أنه لا بأس به
verdicts.en: He did not travel, so he missed the senior shaykhs and contented himself with the scholars of Basra; I hope there is no harm in him.

flags.label: Abu Dawud's reservation
flags.detail: Al-Dhahabi records Abu Dawud as saying “I wrote fifty thousand hadith from him, and were it not for his simplicity I would have left his hadith”, and answers: “more than one declared him reliable” (al-Kashif, as given on the Shamela record). All six compilers took directly from him.

flags.label: The 252 AH cohort
flags.detail: Ibn Hajar writes of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Zaman and Bundar that “the two were like a pair of racehorses, and they died in the same year”, 252 AH (Taqrib, entry 6264). Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, al-Bukhari's shaykh in hadith 15, also died in 252 and was also a teacher of all six.

bio: The Basran who gathered the hadith of his city and taught it to every one of the six compilers; Ibn Khuzaymah called him the imam of his age. He never travelled, which al-Dhahabi notes cost him the senior shaykhs, but his Basran material, above all Ghundar's copy of Shu'bah, made him indispensable. Known everywhere by the laqab Bundar.

provenance.ref: Hady al-Sari, ch. 7, section on those mentioned by laqab

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 7: those mentioned by a laqab (Wikisource)
